abstract: Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) causes heavy yield losses in both sugarcane and maize. However, the hypersensitive cell death (HCD) induced by SCMV helper component proteinase (HC-Pro), an RNA silencing suppressor (RSS), has not been characterized. Here, we show that transient expression of HC-Pro of sugarcane isolate (SCMVSc), but not HC-ProZm of maize isolate (SCMVZm), induces dose-dependent HCD in Nicotiana benthamiana and other plant species. HC-Pro-induced HCD is independent of salicylic acid, reactive oxygen species, and receptor kinases BAK1/SOBIR1, but dependent on Ca2+ influx and helper nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat receptors ADR1/N NRG1. The conserved F345 in HC-Pro is key to HCD induction, whereas the corresponding residue in HC-ProZm is Y345. HC-ProZmY345F induces HCD in N. benthamiana leaves. Correspondingly, SCMVZm-HC-ProY345F-GFP demonstrated markedly decreased infectivity on N. benthamiana and maize compared with SCMVZm-GFP. Furthermore, we show that the interaction between SCMVSc movement protein P3N-PIPO and HC-Pro enhances the RSS activity of HC-Pro and inhibits the intercellular diffusion of silencing signals and HC-Pro-induced HCD, and that the RSS activity of HC-Pro is not required for HCD induction. Together, these findings reveal that SCMV employs different strategies to circumvent HC-Pro-induced HCD in plants, shedding light on the co-evolution mechanisms between SCMV and its hosts sugarcane and maize.
